title: Learning Hamiltonians at Long Times
summary: We study the problem of learning an unknown $n$-qubit Hamiltonian $H$ from $U = e^{-iHt}$ for a single time $t$, where $t$ may be arbitrarily large. For broad families of local Hamiltonians, we prove that, with high probability over $H$ and $t$, any sum of local observables $A$ that is normalized and orthogonal to $H$ satisfies $\tfrac{1}{2^n}\|[U(t),A]\|_F^2 \geq 1/\text{poly}(n)$.
